messages:
elaine: Kicking off Astera -> Redwood migration POC. Customer wants feature parity + zero surprises on billing. main asks: prompt parity, session handoff, and security questionnaire. :wave:
sam: Thanks — can you list the top three compatibility blockers we should show the customer in the POC?
elaine: sure. 1) Astera's session-based streaming with their 'session_id' on every request. 2) different token billing (Astera counts message envelope tokens differently). 3) prompt templating differences (Astera auto-injects system messages).
raj: For (1) we can emulate session_id via our routing metadata. We should document the recommended header mapping: `X-Session-Id -> session_id`. Also show a tiny proxy snippet.
olivia: putting the proxy example here:
```
# example nginx mapping for session header
proxy_set_header X-Session-Id $http_x_session_id;
proxy_pass http://redwood-inference/api/v1/chat
```
raj: For billing, we need to show token mapping. Astera bills tokens including per-message overhead of ~4 tokens; Redwood bills raw model tokens. We'll run sample transcripts to compare delta.
phil: price question from the AE: customer uses 10M tokens/mo on Astera. if we observe a 7% token delta, how do we show cost delta? we should prepare a simple calc table for the POC: tokens_on_customer_history * (redwood_rate/model) * adjustment_factor. I'll draft numbers.
ben: Security QA: they've attached their standard vendor questionnaire (SaaS vendor infosec). I reviewed — main ask is KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts. sec-bot: New file uploaded: /files/astera_poc_security_q_na.pdf :lock: (automated)
elaine: For SOC2 we can provide current report and outline Private deployment option. Need to confirm KMS provider list (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Hashi HSM).
sam: Operational blockers: are there any API surface calls Astera supports that we don't? streaming heartbeats? webhooks?
olivia: Astera exposes a `stream_ack` webhook for partial-delivery confirmations. Redwood doesn't have that exact webhook but supports streaming with chunked SSE and per-chunk metadata. For compatibility demo, we'll run a small shim that translates chunk metadata to a webhook call.
raj: Suggest we prepare two artifacts for the POC deliverable: 1) mapping doc (headers, payload diffs, billing delta calc) 2) small reference shim repo + one-click curl examples.
elaine: I'll own the mapping doc + customer-facing runbook. Raj, can you own the shim repo? Sam — coordinate scheduling with the AE. Phil — pricing delta slides. Ben — security answers + list of artifacts.
sam: noted. ETA for internal dry-run? 48 hours? :calendar:
raj: I can have the shim repo and a smoke test in ~36 hours. It will include: `curl` examples, a node express middleware that rewrites Astera-style messages to Redwood format, and a sample transcript to run billing diffs.
olivia: quick example we can show in the demo of prompt transformation:
```
// Astera payload
{ "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}], "session_id":"abc-123" }
// Redwood target
{ "input": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}], "metadata": {"session_id":"abc-123"} }
```
raj: We'll also include a tiny benchmark that sends 1k messages and compares latency and token count. helps with the customer's SLAs ask.
phil: i'll produce two cost scenarios: matched-throughput and matched-quality (if they pick a higher-capacity model). include committed discount examples for Dedicated.
ben: sec note: they asked about data retention for POC logs. default retention is 30 days; for Private we can set custom retention and a retention SLA. add that to the FAQ.
elaine: great. final customer deliverable checklist: mapping doc, shim repo, billing delta sheet, security pack, runbook, demo script. I'll schedule a dry-run with the AE on Wed.
sam: thanks all — please drop status updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
raj: pushed initial repo skeleton to github.com/redwood/presales-astera-shim (private). will add smoke test next.
elaine: uploaded mapping draft to the drive and pinged the AE. next sync in 48h. :spiral_calendar:
